title: The Significant Music Box
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention. IMPORTANT correction vs. the old lower-fidelity case file: this is NOT a murder or attempted murder. Nobody dies during the present-day case -- Ogata Shuugo (the grandfather) died of illness/old age before the story begins, off-screen, unrelated to any crime. The 'crime' is Kazuko Ogata rigging a scare trap (a koto suspended by thread/hairpin/fan, plus a fake shadow-cutting-in-headlights hoax and threatening pocket-bell messages) to frighten Yuuki Haruna away from digging further into the family's hidden 200-million-yen stamp collection; her son Minoru was injured only by accident when he happened to be in the trapped room in the dark. The old file's culprit ID (s1 = Kazuko) was correct, so label.murderer_id is unchanged, but it should be read as 'principal culprit/trap-setter,' not 'killer.' The old file also entirely omitted: Yuuki Haruna (the visitor whose POV drives the case), Ogata Shirou's parallel subplot of secretly impersonating his dying grandfather via pocket bell for over a year (out of kindness, at the grandfather's own request), the deceased grandfather and grandmother backstory figures, the real solution to the missing-notes puzzle (an Iroha-syllable cipher spelling 'Ihai' / memorial tablet -- the actual hiding place of the stamps, after an initial false lead of 'Model'), and the substitute-koto swap Kazuko used to protect the genuine heirloom. case_type: non-lethal staged-hoax / accidental-injury case with a treasure-hunt subplot.

attrs.resembles: physically/by name reminds the elderly Shuugo Ogata of his own late wife Haruna

attrs.financial_pressure: family finances 'burnt up' on a new kitchen system, a new car, and Minoru's computer; considering selling the music box

houses the koto; ceiling light pull-cord location unfamiliar to guests; site of the koto-drop trap and Minoru's injury

clues.desc: Timeline contradiction: Haruna insists she received the music box in person from 'Shuugo' last Christmas, but Shuugo had been hospitalized and largely immobile since the previous spring and died December 6 -- before that Christmas ever came. Comparing her account against his medical/death timeline proves whoever met her at Shibuya Station was not actually Shuugo.

Behavioral tell: at the front door, Shirou immediately singled out and addressed Haruna specifically, even though the two families had never been introduced and Ran is roughly the same age as her. Comparing that instant recognition against the fact no introduction had occurred implies Shirou already knew what she looked like.

edges.detail: Shuugo began an anonymous pocket-bell friendship with Yuuki Haruna, coincidentally sharing his late wife's name
hospitalized and immobile, Shuugo asks grandson Shirou to look after Haruna in his place, since she reminds him of his late wife
Shirou takes over the pocket-bell correspondence with Haruna in Shuugo's name, out of kindness, without revealing the switch
Shuugo dies of illness at the household, December 6
meets Haruna in person for the only time at Shibuya Station (identifying her by a red muffler), still posing as Shuugo, and gives her the music box and Shuugo's pocket bell
sends 'Cat Burglar!' more than 10 times to Haruna's pocket bell before Haruna ever visits the Ogata house, having grown suspicious after Haruna mentioned collecting stamps
accuses Haruna of coming to the house because Shuugo told her where the family's hidden stamps are
moves the genuine heirloom koto to storage to protect it before rigging the trap
runs to check on the scream and innocently opens the door to Ran's guest room, unwittingly pulling the hairpin and releasing the trap

edges.method: the rigged koto (o3) fell from the ceiling and struck Minoru on the forehead while he was groping for it in the dark, having no idea the room was booby-trapped

edges.detail: removes the paper cutout from the window while the family is occupied with Minoru
sends 'I've been waiting for you, Haruna' to scare her off from returning to the house

edges.motive_type: financial (family finances were exhausted; feared Haruna would find and claim the hidden 200-million-yen stamp collection before the family)
